title: U.S. House · Pennsylvania's 7th Congressional District
area: The Lehigh Valley and part of the Poconos: Lehigh and Northampton counties and part of Monroe County.

context.text: Ballotpedia identified this race as a battleground. Both parties have won the district since 2020: Joe Biden (D) carried it 50%-49% in 2020, Donald Trump (R) carried it 51%-48% in 2024, and Ryan Mackenzie defeated then-incumbent Susan Wild 50%-49% in 2024. As of June 30, 2026, candidates and satellite groups had spent $9.4 million on the race.

Bob Brooks defeated Ryan Crosswell, Lamont McClure, and Carol Obando-Derstine in the May 19, 2026 Democratic primary, winning 41.0% of the vote. Ryan Mackenzie was unopposed in the Republican primary.
Andrew Tupone (Green Party), Ramon Granados (Independent), and Frank Golden (Unaffiliated) withdrew or did not make the general-election ballot, according to Ballotpedia.

summary.text: Ryan Mackenzie is the Republican incumbent U.S. Representative for Pennsylvania's 7th District, first elected in 2024 when he defeated then-incumbent Susan Wild. A Lehigh Valley resident, he previously worked in state government and served in the Pennsylvania House of Representatives from 2012 to 2024. In Congress he serves on the Education and Workforce, Foreign Affairs and Homeland Security committees and chairs the Workforce Protections Subcommittee. His campaign website describes him as running on tax relief, health care costs and housing affordability.

background.text: According to his official biography, Mackenzie is a ninth-generation resident of the Lehigh Valley, where his family has lived since colonial times.
Graduated from Parkland High School in 2000, earned a bachelor's degree in finance and international business from New York University in 2004, and an M.B.A. from Harvard in 2010.

Before elected office, worked at the U.S. Department of Labor in the Office of the Secretary, on political campaigns, and as policy director at the Pennsylvania Department of Labor and Industry; he also earned a real estate sales license.
Won a special election on April 24, 2012 for Pennsylvania House District 134 and was re-elected in later cycles; he later represented District 187 after redistricting (2022-2024).
In the state House he was Republican chair of the Labor & Industry Committee and co-chair of the International Relations Caucus; his official biography says he authored a dozen laws.
Elected to the U.S. House on November 5, 2024, defeating incumbent Democrat Susan Wild by a margin of 50% to 49%, according to Ballotpedia.
Serves on the Education and Workforce, Foreign Affairs and Homeland Security committees and chairs the Workforce Protections Subcommittee.

Has served on nonprofit and government boards, including local organizations for senior housing and autism services, Lehigh Career & Technical Institute, the Greater Lehigh Valley Chamber of Commerce, state workforce and economic development boards, and the President's Commission on White House Fellowships.
Lives in the Lehigh Valley with his wife, Chloe, and their children, according to his official biography.

priorities.text: Campaign platform lists 12 priorities, including delivering tax relief, safeguarding Social Security and Medicare, improving housing affordability, reducing health care costs, and securing the border.

Says his first package of bills in Congress included proposals on the Child Tax Credit and childcare tax credits, some of which were included in the "Working Families Tax Cuts," and that he continues to work "across the aisle to support a host of commonsense legislative initiatives that make life easier for working families."
priorities.quote: The very first package of bills Ryan introduced in Congress included proposals to the Child Tax Credit, childcare tax credits, and more. While Congressman Mackenzie was able to include these ideas in the Working Families Tax Cuts, he's not done yet – continuing to team with legislators from across the aisle to support a host of commonsense legislative initiatives that make life easier for working families.

priorities.text: Says he is focused on reducing the cost of living through housing, transportation, and energy permitting legislation.
priorities.quote: We're continuing to work on housing legislation, transportation legislation, energy permitting legislation. All those things can help bring down costs in the long-term.

positions.summary: Says he has secured millions of dollars to support law enforcement and first responders and will continue to work with law enforcement on public-safety legislation.
positions.quote: he has secured millions of dollars to better support law enforcement and first responders, as well as passed important laws that secure our borders and combat the illegal drug trade

positions.summary: His 2026 campaign priorities page lists opposing the participation of transgender athletes in women’s sports, in the wording quoted.
His April 2024 campaign priorities page said he supports constitutional carry and opposes efforts to confiscate firearms without due process.
positions.quote: Support constitutional carry and oppose far-left efforts to confiscate firearms without due process.

positions.summary: His April 2024 campaign priorities page called for hiring more law enforcement officers, including funding for CBP and ICE.
positions.quote: Hire and retain more law enforcement officers – including funding for U.S. Customs and Border protection (CBP) and Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE)

positions.summary: His April 2024 campaign priorities page said he opposes cap-and-tax proposals and supports expanded American energy exploration, extraction and production.
positions.quote: Oppose cap-and-tax schemes that prioritize a radical climate agenda over the realities of safe, clean, affordable American energy.

record.text: Assigned to the Committee on Homeland Security, the Committee on Education and the Workforce (where he chairs a subcommittee), and the Committee on Foreign Affairs in the 2025-2026 Congress.
Says he introduced a package of bills including proposals for an expanded Child Tax Credit and childcare tax credits, and that provisions were incorporated into the "Working Families Tax Cuts."
Elected to the U.S. House in 2024, defeating incumbent Susan Wild 50.4% to 49.4%.

candidates.name: Bob Brooks
candidates.ballotNote: Won the May 19 Democratic primary with 41.0% of the vote
candidates.currentRole: Former President, Pennsylvania Professional Fire Fighters Association

summary.text: Bob Brooks is the Democratic nominee for Pennsylvania's 7th District. He worked as a Bethlehem firefighter from 2005 to 2025 and has been president of the Pennsylvania Professional Fire Fighters Association since 2021. He won the May 19, 2026 Democratic primary; his campaign describes a focus on affordability, health care and opposition to the One Big Beautiful Bill Act.

background.text: According to his campaign website, Brooks was raised primarily by a single mother who worked as a bartender, and he moved to Pennsylvania more than 30 years ago.
According to his campaign website, before becoming a firefighter he held jobs including dishwasher, short-order cook, bartender, landscaper, warehouse worker and pizza delivery driver, and Teamster.
Worked as a firefighter in Bethlehem, Pennsylvania, from 2005 to 2025, and retired from the department in 2025.
Held multiple positions in his firefighters' union, and was elected president of the Pennsylvania Professional Fire Fighters Association in 2021.
According to his campaign website, he helped lead a campaign to pass mental health coverage for firefighters with post-traumatic stress.
Started Brooks Lawn Care, a snow removal and lawn care business, in 2013.
Has coached youth and varsity baseball at Nazareth Area High School; according to his campaign website he lives in Nazareth with his wife, Jen.
Announced his candidacy on August 26, 2025 as the fifth Democrat in the race, with no prior elected office, and won the primary on May 19, 2026.

priorities.text: Lists affordability, health care (restoring Medicaid cuts and "Medicare for All"), housing, childcare, and utilities as his three key campaign messages, along with protecting Social Security and enforcing antitrust rules.
priorities.quote: The number one thing I hear from folks is how expensive life is. People can't keep up with groceries, rent, healthcare, childcare, or utility bills. Wages aren't keeping up, and too many are working harder than ever for too little.

priorities.text: Says he wants to take money out of politics, end stock trading in Congress, enforce term limits, and make the wealthy pay their fair share.
priorities.quote: We need to take money out of politics, end stock trading in Congress, enforce term limits, and make the wealthy pay their fair share.

priorities.text: Names wages, safe working conditions, the social safety net, health care, and affordable housing as the public-policy areas he is most passionate about.

positions.summary: Supports restoring Medicaid cuts made under the One Big Beautiful Bill Act and providing "Medicare for All."
positions.quote: Healthcare: Restore Medicaid cuts and provide Medicare for All.

positions.summary: Supports repealing Head Start cuts and expanding childcare subsidies and publicly funded preschool.
positions.quote: Childcare: Repeal Headstart cuts, expand subsidies and publicly funded preschool.

positions.summary: His campaign platform calls for a billionaire minimum tax and repealing the 2017 tax cuts for billionaires and big corporations.
positions.quote: We need to pass a billionaire minimum tax: a baseline tax rate the ultra-wealthy can’t dodge.

positions.summary: His campaign platform supports building more starter homes and, in some cases, cutting rules and red tape that make homes harder to build.
positions.quote: And yes, sometimes cut rules and red tape that make it harder and more expensive to get homes built.

positions.summary: His campaign platform calls for codifying Roe v. Wade and passing legislation to overturn state abortion bans.
positions.quote: We need to codify Roe v. Wade and pass legislation to overturn Trump abortion bans in red states.

positions.summary: His campaign platform calls for universal background checks, closing the gun show loophole and enforcing waiting periods, while saying he respects the Second Amendment.
positions.quote: We need common-sense laws: universal background checks, closing the gun show loophole, and enforcing waiting periods so dangerous people don’t get their hands on guns.

positions.summary: His campaign platform calls for bringing back renewables cut by the Trump administration and building wind and solar projects, alongside new nuclear and natural gas plants.
positions.quote: Bring back renewables cut by Trump, invest in new nuclear and natural gas power plants, and crack down on price-gouging utility monopolies.

positions.summary: His campaign platform calls for raising the minimum wage and tying it to inflation.
positions.quote: We need to raise it, and tie it to inflation.

positions.summary: His campaign platform says he will not support using federal money for vouchers to private schools.
positions.quote: I will not support using federal money to hand vouchers to private schools while public schools are being starved.

positions.summary: Spotlight PA reports he criticizes tariffs in campaign materials as raising prices and hurting small businesses.
positions.quote: taking money out of working people's pockets, raising prices and making it harder for small businesses to survive.

candidates.researchNotes: No official record items included; Brooks has not held elected office. Positions are drawn from his Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey response.
